Maths at work

Catering and hospitality

Jobs in this route, and the maths they use.

Percentages

Baker

Catering and hospitality

\(\displaystyle \text{water} = 70\% \times \text{flour}\)

How much water for 500 g of flour?

Bakers write recipes in "baker's percentages": the flour is always 100%, and everything else is a percentage of the flour's weight. A dough is 70% water and 2% salt. You use 500 g of flour.

  1. Water: \(70\% \text{ of } 500 = 0.7 \times 500 = 350\) g.
  2. Salt: \(2\% \text{ of } 500 = 0.02 \times 500 = 10\) g.

The answer: \(0.7 \times 500 = 350\) g of water

Indices and exponential change

Chef

Catering and hospitality

\(\displaystyle N = 100 \times 2^n\)

n is the number of 20-minute doublings

Why is food left out for 2 hours thrown away?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Hot food must be kept at 63°C or above. Below that, bacteria can double every 20 minutes in the right conditions, which is why food left out more than 2 hours is thrown away. Start with 100 bacteria, 2 hours at room temperature (example figure):

  1. Doublings: \(120 \div 20 = 6\).
  2. Bacteria: \(100 \times 2^{6} = 100 \times 64 = 6{,}400\).

The answer: \(100 \times 2^{6} = 6{,}400\) bacteria
